title: Harness self-check: the section H continuous recorder, device-named presses and the restoration checks
_comment: NOT a protocol segment. Evidence for the section 1.5 follow-up: record_start/record_stop, the device argument on press, and the four restoration assert checks. Boots the TITLE rather than the Meadows -- a cold world stand-up costs ~95 s on this container and nothing about whether the recorder writes PNGs at a cadence is answered better by a heavier scene. pin_clock is exercised by the DIAG world segments, since a title screen has no WorldLook to pin.
_comment_baseline: record_hz is declared at 0.5 Hz here so the baseline itself is visible in frames/manifest.json before any record_start step runs. A journey segment would declare 0.1.

steps.title: boot the real title screen
steps.expected: the real title comes up; the recorder is already running at the segment baseline of 0.5 Hz

steps.title: let the baseline record a few frames
steps.expected: about three background frames at 0.5 Hz, filed under frames/selfcheck_record/, with no step having asked for them

steps.title: raise the rate for a window
steps.expected: the background rate goes to 4 Hz and recording continues across the steps below without blocking them

steps.title: move focus on the PAD while recording
steps.expected: the joypad binding is injected explicitly; frames keep being written underneath the presses

steps.title: move focus on the KEYBOARD
steps.expected: the keyboard binding is injected. Before `device` existed this action resolved to its pad binding and the KBM half of section L.1 was unreachable while the cell read as covered.

steps.title: something still holds focus
steps.expected: the title still has a focused button after presses on two different devices

steps.title: a device the action does not bind
steps.expected: FAIL naming the verb and the device. Not a fallback to the pad: an unreachable verb on a device is a real answer for the matrix, and a silent fallback is how this stayed invisible.

steps.title: the mouse is not captured at the title
steps.expected: the title screen is a mouse-visible surface. The same check verdicts section E.4's requirement that the pause shell RESTORES capture on close.

steps.title: a capture step, mid-window

args.intended_proof: a prescribed section G shot taken inside an open recording window: it lands in shots/, the recorder stands down for it, and `hud` is stored verbatim rather than coerced to on/off

steps.expected: one PNG in shots/ with hud recorded as "as shipped"; no frames/ file for the same instant

steps.title: keep recording after the shot
steps.expected: the window is still open at 4 Hz and the recorder resumes after the capture step

steps.title: end the window
steps.expected: back to the segment baseline of 0.5 Hz -- not off, because section H's record is continuous and a window ending is not the segment ending

steps.title: the baseline is still recording
steps.expected: background frames continue at 0.5 Hz after the window closed

steps.title: close the segment

args.text: frames/manifest.json holds the whole cadence: baseline rows, a 4 Hz window, event-forced rows, and no row sharing an instant with the shots/ capture

steps.expected: a note event closes the segment, and forces a frame of its own
